953 AM EDT Fri Oct 9 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Have added mention of the isolated tornado risk on Day 3/Sunday
as the remnants of Isaias track through. Otherwise, will
continue to monitor the 12Z guidance for any needed updates.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Remnants of Hurricane Isaias to bring rain, breezy 
  conditions Sunday into Sunday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Remnants of Hurricane Isaias to bring rain, 
breezy conditions Sunday into Sunday night.

The pattern remains quiet through the first half of the weekend
as surface high pressure strengthens over the northeastern U.S.
However, this lengthy period of tranquil weather will come to an
end as this ridge retreats northward ahead of Isaias. Until
then, a thick area of high cirrus should continue to track
poleward. Daily highs will be in the low/mid 70s, with 60s
across mountain locations.

The main weather impact to the region over the next week is going to 
be from the remnants of what is now Hurricane Isaias (Cat 3
strength). Model guidance is in generally good agreement that 
Hurricane Isaias' surface low weakens and broadens as the system
moves into the TN Valley Saturday night into Sunday. The mid-
level circulation amplifies and becomes a strong cutoff low over
KY/TN that moves slowly east across the Mid- Atlantic Sunday 
into Monday. Periods of rain are likely across the area at times
Saturday evening through Sunday night. Rainfall amounts of 1-2 
inches are expected across the area. Higher rain totals are 
certainly possible, but will depend on a few other smaller scale
features.

Tropical moisture surges north into our area Saturday night into 
Sunday, with the highest PWAT values at or above 2" (most likely 
east of the Blue Ridge). While the main cutoff low associated with 
the remnants of Isaias remain west of the Appalachians on Saturday, 
expect light rain to move in from south to north in the evening. 
Forcing for ascent increases Saturday night, and especially Sunday 
morning into Sunday afternoon as mid-level heights fall with the 
approach of the cutoff low. There is going to be enhanced low-level 
convergence somewhere over the region as the surface high to the 
east and cutoff low to the west interact. Easterly flow into the 
Blue Ridge could also produce enhanced rain amounts due to 
orographic effects. Additionally, an inverted trough or wave of low 
pressure tries to develop in lee of the Appalachians Sunday as it 
crosses Virginia to the Delmarva.

Uncertainty remains regarding the exact evolution and timing of 
these features, which will ultimately determine where / if any 
locally heavy rain occurs. Continue to monitor the forecast over the 
next couple of days. No Flood Watches are planned at this time as we 
are still over 48 hours from the main slug of rain.
Additionally, there is a non-zero risk of isolated tornadoes on
Sunday. These post-tropical environments can be tricky as low-
level spin ups do occur. For now, the Storm Prediction Center
has maintained a Day 3 Marginal Risk area.

It is going to be noticeably breezy, especially in the mountains 
where winds begin to pick up Saturday evening. The strongest winds 
are most likely on Sunday. The current forecast for peak wind gusts 
is 30-40 mph in the Alleghenies and 20-30 mph elsewhere.

Conditions dry out Monday morning into Monday afternoon as the 
remnants of Isaias push offshore. Looking at mostly mild 
temperatures for most of next week. A series of cold fronts cross 
the region during the middle to late part of next week as the 
synoptic pattern becomes more active. Aside from mountain rain 
showers, most of the area looks to remain dry. The strongest cold 
front arrives late next week, possibly bringing rain and colder air 
behind it.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected through Saturday. Sub-VFR conditions are 
expected at some time Saturday night into Sunday as the remnants of 
what is now Hurricane Isaias move through the area. Low clouds and 
reduced visibility due to steady rain are going to be the main 
impacts. Breezy east winds gusting around 20 knots is likely on 
Sunday. VFR conditions return Monday and Tuesday.

&&

.MARINE...
Favorable marine conditions are expected through Saturday afternoon. 
Then, SCA conditions are likely to develop across all the waters 
Saturday evening into Sunday as easterly flow increases. The 
remnants of what is now Hurricane Isaias will move across the waters 
Sunday, which is when gusts of around 30 knots are likely. 
Conditions improve Monday, though passing cold fronts next week will 
bring the opportunity for SCA conditions at times.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Minor coastal flooding seems likely at sensitive locations Sunday 
evening due to rising water levels due to strengthening east to 
southeast winds combined with high astronomical tides due to a new 
moon. Based on the latest forecast, Annapolis could near
moderate flooding levels on Sunday evening, but confidence is
low at this time. Winds turn offshore Monday allowing tide 
levels to recede.
